YES

The script drops blocks {2, 6, 10, 14}, builds `renumber` from the ordered surviving list (0→0, 1→1, 3→2, … 15→11, matching the spec's mapping exactly), and rewrites only the index portion of each key while keeping the tensor object, so values, shapes and dtypes are untouched. Non-block tensors (`model.embed_tokens.weight`, `lm_head.weight`) fall through the `fullmatch is None` branch unchanged. Writing into a fresh dict under new names avoids the collision hazard entirely. Both assertions — layer index set equals `{0..11}` (which also establishes that no block 12–15 remains) and total tensor count equals 86 — run before `save_file`, so a failure exits non-zero with no output written.
